Who invented the telephone? The British say Alexander Graham Bell. The Americans say Antonio Meucci. The Germans are not having it: it was clearly their own Philipp Reis. In this contest, Bell has the textbooks on his side, including Chinese ones, and Meucci has the US Congress, which settled the matter in his favor. Reis remains little known, perhaps because of German modesty.

2020 was declared the International Year of Sound, and the modest Reis may still have felt a little hard done by. So, in this short promotional film, he travels through time in the style of the Netflix series Dark, from 1860 to 2020, arriving in Aachen in western Germany, the city of Charlemagne, who is said to be the King of Hearts in a deck of cards. There he meets his acoustical colleague 160 years on, Professor Michael Vorländer.

Main video sources: Dark; DEGA e.V. (the German Acoustical Society). Shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
